## ERE-C0001 — Typed and sourced requirement meaning

### Identity

**Property id.** ERE-C0001

**Property name.** Typed and sourced requirement meaning

**Lineage id.** EVOLVED_REQUIREMENTS_ENGINEERING

**Property families.** ERE-FAM01

**Record kind.** CANDIDATE_OR_RETAINED_MECHANISM

**Parent ids.** None recorded.

**Alias or supersession ids.** None recorded.

**Discovery source ids.** ERE-S-F004; ERE-S-F008; ERE-S-F007

**Native family labels.** ERE-BR-F02

### Genealogy

**Historical origin.** Competing environment-property, intentional and necessary-feature definitions; no single original meaning.

**Original terminology.** The relevant native distinctions are indicative domain statements, optative requirements and specifications (ERE-S-F004, manuscript §§3.1–3.2, pp.6–9), and beliefs, desires, intentions and attitudes in a revised requirements ontology (ERE-S-F008, introduction and §4, pp.7–8). 'Typed and sourced requirement meaning' is this packet's cross-source mechanism label, not either paper's original term.

**Original form.** See exact source/version profiles; the candidate label is a researcher normalization, not an invented historical quotation.

**Original problem.** ERE-S-F004 asks how requirements, specifications and domain descriptions can be related without treating the machine alone as the subject of all requirements (§§3.1–3.2 and §5, pp.20–23). ERE-S-F008 asks whether the earlier requirements problem represents the kinds of concern stakeholders communicate, including preferences and quality concerns (§4, pp.7–8). The packet combines those questions; it does not attribute one common original problem statement to both papers.

**Branch ids.** ERE-BR-F02

**Influence or relation class.** Documented source links distinguished from researcher comparisons in genealogy_edges.

**Historical evidence and locators.** **Claim id.** ERE-S-F004-CL01

**Source id.** ERE-S-F004

**Locator.** Manuscript §§3.1–3.2, pp.6–9; §5, pp.20–23

**Role.** Mechanism/history or bounded contrary evidence; inspect source ceiling.

**Claim id.** ERE-S-F008-CL01

**Source id.** ERE-S-F008

**Locator.** §4 revised requirements problem, pp.7–8 manuscript

**Role.** Mechanism/history or bounded contrary evidence; inspect source ceiling.

**Claim id.** ERE-S-F007-CL01

**Source id.** ERE-S-F007

**Locator.** §2 solution overlap argument; §3 limitations

**Role.** Mechanism/history or bounded contrary evidence; inspect source ceiling.

**Disputed attribution or anachronism risk.** Do not back-project later tool semantics or current vocabulary into earlier papers; see source access/version notes.

### Claim and mechanism

**Engineering claim.** A material statement must be interpreted by its semantic role and source before it can support a downstream obligation.

**Claim class.** QUALITATIVE_REVIEW

**Bearer or subject.** A requirement-bearing statement and its decision context

**Failure mode or limit addressed.** An observed staff workaround is relabeled mandatory simply because it occurs often.

**Mechanism.** Separate observations, desires, agreed constraints, preferences and implementation hypotheses; record the reason for treating each as binding or defeasible.

**Mature or evolved form.** **Predicate ref.** ERE-C0001-P01

**Interpretation.** Typed and sourced requirement meaning

**Expected payoff.** Decision-relevant reduction of the failure described in this record; a rationale rather than an invented measured effect.

**Payoff evidence not just rationale.** Conceptual distinctions and criticism; no causal estimate of benefits from this particular profile.

**Decision or consumer.** Ambiguous use of shall, goal, requirement or constraint changes a decision

**Alternative mechanisms.** A short explanation, concrete examples, or a targeted review can implement the mechanism without adopting its historical notation.

### Applicability and authority

**Trigger or context.** Ambiguous use of shall, goal, requirement or constraint changes a decision

**Non trigger or cheap path.** A single clear request with named requester and examples may need only a short note

**Assumptions and preconditions.** Statement source and relevant decision scope are available; classifications may be plural

**Environment and boundary.** A requirement-bearing statement and its decision context; Interpretation at the named version and decision; no logical operator creates normative authority.

**Scope and exclusions.** Typing does not establish truth, legitimacy, feasibility or stakeholder coverage.

**Authority or normative basis if applicable.** The proposer, affected parties and actual decision right must be identified independently of grammatical modality

**Input and evidence provenance requirements.** Actual statement/model, source identity, version, interpretation and evidence for both named attributes; source literature is not evidence that a particular target satisfies them.

**Dependencies and conflicts.** ERE-T-F01

**Failure of assumptions.** Reopen the affected conditional conclusion; do not infer the external obligation was fulfilled.

**Cost and maintenance burden.** Small for a few consequential statements; expensive if every sentence is classified mechanically

**Retirement or reentry condition.** Retire when the triggering decision or obligation ends; re-enter on changed boundary, interpretation, actors, assumptions or interface.

### Criticism and evolution

**Criticism ids.** ERE-CR-F01

**Strongest objection.** Classification can become bureaucratic and source actors can disagree about meaning.

**Known failures and misuses.** An observed staff workaround is relabeled mandatory simply because it occurs often.

**Response or descendant form.** **Mechanism ref.** ERE-C0001.CLAIM_AND_MECHANISM.MECHANISM

**What changed and what did not.** The scoped mechanism/decision rule is retained where justified; neither actual-domain truth nor social authority is supplied by its representation.

**Residual limits.** Typing does not establish truth, legitimacy, feasibility or stakeholder coverage.

**Ceremony versus mechanism.** A single clear request with named requester and examples may need only a short note

**Internal tension ids.** ERE-T-F01

**Retention status.** RETAINED_IN_EVOLVED_FORM

**Retention rationale.** The scoped claim and strongest objection above determine this status; the empirical and formal partitions remain separate.

## ERE-C0002 — Alternative-bounded necessity claims

### Identity

**Property id.** ERE-C0002

**Property name.** Alternative-bounded necessity claims

**Lineage id.** EVOLVED_REQUIREMENTS_ENGINEERING

**Property families.** ERE-FAM01

**Record kind.** CANDIDATE_OR_RETAINED_MECHANISM

**Parent ids.** None recorded.

**Alias or supersession ids.** None recorded.

**Discovery source ids.** ERE-S-F007; ERE-S-F008; ERE-S-F036

**Native family labels.** ERE-BR-F02

### Genealogy

**Historical origin.** The necessary-feature critique exposes scope hidden by the word requirement.

**Original terminology.** ERE-S-F007 uses design object, feature, goal, and a deliberately narrow definition of requirement as a feature necessary for a goal (§§1–2, especially §2's alternative-design argument). ERE-S-F008 uses the revised requirements problem with preferences (§4, pp.7–8). 'Alternative-bounded necessity' is an analyst label for a qualification, not a source-native school or theorem name.

**Original form.** See exact source/version profiles; the candidate label is a researcher normalization, not an invented historical quotation.

**Original problem.** ERE-S-F007 challenges the inference that known successful designs establish necessary features: alternatives can lack common features, and unexamined alternatives prevent knowing that a feature is indispensable (§2; limitations in §3). ERE-S-F008 addresses the further problem of selecting acceptable specifications when stakeholder preferences and quality concerns matter (§4). The issue is the scope and warrant of a necessity claim, not a claim that all commitments are illusory.

**Branch ids.** ERE-BR-F02

**Influence or relation class.** Documented source links distinguished from researcher comparisons in genealogy_edges.

**Historical evidence and locators.** **Claim id.** ERE-S-F007-CL01

**Source id.** ERE-S-F007

**Locator.** §2 solution overlap argument; §3 limitations

**Role.** Mechanism/history or bounded contrary evidence; inspect source ceiling.

**Claim id.** ERE-S-F008-CL01

**Source id.** ERE-S-F008

**Locator.** §4 revised requirements problem, pp.7–8 manuscript

**Role.** Mechanism/history or bounded contrary evidence; inspect source ceiling.

**Claim id.** ERE-S-F036-CL01

**Source id.** ERE-S-F036

**Locator.** §2 domains/descriptions; §§7.1,7.4,7.5 concerns

**Role.** Mechanism/history or bounded contrary evidence; inspect source ceiling.

**Disputed attribution or anachronism risk.** Do not back-project later tool semantics or current vocabulary into earlier papers; see source access/version notes.

### Claim and mechanism

**Engineering claim.** Treat necessity as relative to an outcome, an explicit alternative set and justified constraints; distinguish a chosen solution commitment.

**Claim class.** RESEARCHER_FORMALISATION

**Bearer or subject.** A necessity claim for feature f under objective O and feasible alternatives X

**Failure mode or limit addressed.** A web portal is called necessary although a staffed telephone process could meet the stated access objective.

**Mechanism.** Seek a materially different outcome-achieving alternative before declaring a feature unavoidable; preserve uncertainty about unexplored alternatives.

**Mature or evolved form.** **Predicate ref.** ERE-C0002-P01

**Interpretation.** Alternative-bounded necessity claims

**Expected payoff.** Decision-relevant reduction of the failure described in this record; a rationale rather than an invented measured effect.

**Payoff evidence not just rationale.** Ralph supplies a conceptual counterargument; no effect estimate. Empirical framing lead retained but unread body prevents transfer.

**Decision or consumer.** A proposed implementation feature is defended as the only way to meet a need

**Alternative mechanisms.** A short explanation, concrete examples, or a targeted review can implement the mechanism without adopting its historical notation.

### Applicability and authority

**Trigger or context.** A proposed implementation feature is defended as the only way to meet a need

**Non trigger or cheap path.** For a fixed external interface, record the legitimate constraint and avoid reopening every design choice

**Assumptions and preconditions.** Alternatives are comparable for the specified outcome; success and exclusion constraints are declared

**Environment and boundary.** A necessity claim for feature f under objective O and feasible alternatives X; Quantification is over declared alternatives, not all possible solutions or all future worlds.

**Scope and exclusions.** Success probabilities and social legitimacy are not captured by simple set intersection.

**Authority or normative basis if applicable.** Decision makers can select a design without proving universal necessity; selection and necessity are different claims

**Input and evidence provenance requirements.** Actual statement/model, source identity, version, interpretation and evidence for both named attributes; source literature is not evidence that a particular target satisfies them.

**Dependencies and conflicts.** ERE-T-F01

**Failure of assumptions.** Reopen the affected conditional conclusion; do not infer the external obligation was fulfilled.

**Cost and maintenance burden.** Exploration can be costly and indefinite; stop against decision-relevant alternatives, not all imaginable futures

**Retirement or reentry condition.** Retire when the triggering decision or obligation ends; re-enter on changed boundary, interpretation, actors, assumptions or interface.

### Genealogy

**Historical origin.** Four-variable functional documentation and environment-oriented RE developed related, differently partitioned boundary models.

**Original terminology.** Requirements, specifications, domain properties, shared phenomena and indicative/optative descriptions are native terms in ERE-S-F004 (§§3.1–3.2 and §5). Monitored/controlled quantities and the descriptions linking them to program inputs/outputs occur in ERE-S-F003 (§§4.2–4.4). ERE-S-F005 supplies a reference model relating environment, machine and specification (§3, equations (1)–(3); §4.1, equations (4)–(8)). The packet's property label joins these related accounts without treating their notation as identical.

**Original form.** See exact source/version profiles; the candidate label is a researcher normalization, not an invented historical quotation.

**Original problem.** The sources seek to show how specified computer behavior can justify a required change in the surrounding world when observations, actuators and domain knowledge intervene. Functional documentation must distinguish the quantities involved (ERE-S-F003, §§4.2–4.4), while a requirements argument needs a sound relation between domain knowledge, specification and required outcome (ERE-S-F004, §5; ERE-S-F005, §§3–5). The historical motivation is the missing semantic bridge, not the later objection that a model may encode the wrong world.

### Claim and mechanism

**Engineering claim.** A machine-level claim supports an external requirement only through explicit, defensible domain and interface assumptions.

**Failure mode or limit addressed.** The alarm code is correct while a stuck sensor destroys the assumed connection to actual temperature.

**Interpretation.** World–machine sufficiency with correspondence obligations

**Expected payoff.** Decision-relevant reduction of the failure described in this record; a rationale rather than an invented measured effect.

**Payoff evidence not just rationale.** Source theories establish conditional relations; examples demonstrate failure mechanisms, not field reliability rates.

'Observation- and control-compatible responsibility' is the packet's normalized name. Its separate researcher screen is not the source's complete realizability definition.

**Failure mode or limit addressed.** Two worlds look identical to the agent but require mutually exclusive immediate actions.

**Mechanism.** Compare histories indistinguishable to the actor; identify any requirement for incompatible outputs or unavailable actions, then change allocation, sensors, actuators or goal scope explicitly.

### Applicability and authority

**Trigger or context.** A task is assigned across a boundary with hidden conditions or external intervention

**Assumptions and preconditions.** Faithful observation timing and control boundary; declare the selected check. Source assignability, actual responsibility consistency, general causal strategy and actual authority are distinct. See ERE-C0004-P01.

**Scope and exclusions.** The source assignability witness is distinct from the actual implementation. A stronger actual implementation is not rejected solely for admitting fewer goal histories. These model checks establish neither operational capability nor authority; use ERE-C0008 for its separately declared causal-strategy question.

**Authority or normative basis if applicable.** Technical control is not permission; authorization of real actors requires separate evidence

**Failure of assumptions.** Reopen the affected conditional conclusion; do not infer the external obligation was fulfilled.

### Predicates, witnesses and evaluation

**Predicate specifications.** **Predicate id.** ERE-C0004-P01

**Property id.** ERE-C0004

**Name and plain language claim.** Observation- and control-compatible responsibility

**Predicate kind.** MATHEMATICAL_MODEL_PROPERTY

**Subject and argument signature.** Check(kind, ag, G, Mon, Ctrl, history_universe, Δ_witness?, Δ_actual?); kind is NECESSARY_INFORMATION_SCREEN, KAOS_2002_ASSIGNABILITY or ACTUAL_RESPONSIBILITY_CONSISTENCY.

**Variable domains and units.** **Kind.** One explicitly selected check; do not combine its verdict with the others without stating the conjunction.

**Ag.** Agent whose interface declares disjoint Mon(ag) and Ctrl(ag) sets of state variables.

**G.** Goal interpreted over the common system-state history universe.

**State(v).** Valuations of the variables V; model-structural, no numerical unit implied.

**Path(v).** Sequences of valuations of V, with observed prefixes used for next-state decisions.

**Δ.** Candidate transition system <Init,Next>: Init⊆State(Ctrl(ag)); Next⊆Path(Mon(ag)∪Ctrl(ag))×State(Ctrl(ag)), total on its source-model path domain.

**Run δ(ag).** Infinite system-state runs induced by the candidate Δ under the F012 conventions; distinct from RUN_Δactual(ag).

**Hist(g).** All system-state histories permitted by G in that same universe.

**Δ actual.** The actual modeled implementation; not the variable existentially quantified in source assignability.

**Observation equivalence.** A01 relation over admitted prefixes at the decision time, used in the separate researcher screen.

**Action capability.** A02 available actions/next controlled valuations. For the screen, A_G(h,t) denotes actions compatible with the goal at prefix h and time t under the selected model.

**Quantifiers and scope.** KAOS_2002_ASSIGNABILITY: ∃Δ compatible with the declared interface such that RUN_Δ(ag)=HIST(G). ACTUAL_RESPONSIBILITY_CONSISTENCY: Responsible(ag,G) implies ∀r∈RUN_Δactual(ag), r∈HIST(G); this does not quantify over a new actual implementation or require equality. NECESSARY_INFORMATION_SCREEN: ∀decision times t and admitted prefixes h1,h2, observation-equivalent prefixes must not require disjoint available action sets. Passing this pairwise necessary screen is not a complete synthesis or assignability proof.

**State trace event or model bearer.** Separate possible witness transition system, actual transition system and goal histories under a declared common model; finite prefix examples illustrate distinctions but do not replace the infinite-run source semantics.

**Temporal and modal semantics.** The F012 agent model uses initial controlled states and a total next-state relation based on monitored/controlled histories, inducing infinite runs. Its existential witness is a capability claim under that model. Actual responsibility uses inclusion; C0008 retains its independently specified causal-strategy semantics and C0007 its operationalization semantics.

**Assumptions.** Faithful observation timing and control boundary; declare the selected check. Source assignability, actual responsibility consistency, general causal strategy and actual authority are distinct. See ERE-C0004-P01.

**Applicability guard.** An allocation or responsibility conclusion relies on an actor’s observation/control boundary; declare the check kind and model. ACTUAL_RESPONSIBILITY_CONSISTENCY applies only when Responsible(ag,G) is asserted; an unassigned goal does not receive a favorable consistency verdict.

**Expression or precise operational rule.** Use the declared kind. (1) Researcher necessary screen: if h1 and h2 have the same observations at t but A_G(h1,t)∩A_G(h2,t)=∅, the proposed guaranteed allocation fails that screen. Its converse is not claimed. (2) F012 assignability: ∃Δ=<Init,Next> compatible with Mon/Ctrl and the source agent model, with RUN_Δ(ag)=HIST(G). (3) Actual responsibility consistency: Responsible(ag,G) ⇒ RUN_Δactual(ag)⊆HIST(G). For several assigned goals check actual inclusion for each; a proper subset for one goal is allowed. Do not test (2) by substituting Δ_actual for the existentially quantified Δ.

**Fail.** An exhibited indistinguishable-prefix/disjoint-action pair defeats the screen; a sound source-model impossibility argument defeats assignability; an actual run outside HIST(G) defeats responsibility consistency. Actual strict inclusion alone is not a failure.

**Unknown.** The claimed check lacks a justified model, witness/proof, actual-run description or load-bearing observation/control evidence. Passing only a finite screen leaves a stronger assignability claim unknown.

**Inapplicable.** No guaranteed allocation/control claim invokes this boundary, or the particular source model is not the chosen semantics; name the applicable cheaper check instead.

**Predicate id.** ERE-C0006-P02

**Property id.** ERE-C0006

**Name and plain language claim.** Model-conditional probabilistic satisfaction threshold: the estimated nonvacuous goal satisfaction rate in a declared obstacle model meets its required minimum.

**Predicate kind.** PROBABILISTIC_OR_STATISTICAL_CLAIM

**Subject and argument signature.** P02(G,M,q), where G is a behavioral goal, M is a versioned finite behavior/probability model with an explicit triggering condition C and temporal consequent H_G, and q is its prescribed satisfaction threshold.

**Variable domains and units.** **G.** Behavioral goal C implies H_G in declared finite-trace temporal semantics.

**M.** (Omega,D,mu,C,H_G,obstacle/refinement assertions,parameter provenance). Omega is a finite behavior-episode space; mu is a normalized probability measure. The source's unweighted finite count is the equal-weight case.

**Q.** Real probability 0<q<1, supplied by A04.

**P m.** mu(C intersect H_G)/mu(C), dimensionless; mu(C)>0.

**Theta.** Optional uncertain probability parameters with an explicit joint epistemic law Pi; Pi is not the operational measure mu.

**Sv.** q-p_M, a signed probability-point gap, not a cost or harm measure.

**Quantifiers and scope.** One named goal, version, trigger, environment regime and finite horizon. Compare the probability over all episodes in the declared conditional model; no universal statement over other deployments or future environments. If multiple parameter models are retained, report each result or conservative bounds, rather than silently select a favorable model.

**State trace event or model bearer.** A probability-bearing finite behavior model plus a separately supplied normative threshold.

**Temporal and modal semantics.** H_G retains the goal's deadline/temporal interpretation. Episodes with C false do not count as successes. A finite run cannot establish an unbounded eventuality without a separate model. PASS means true in the specified probability model, not an observed guarantee over all real executions.

**Assumptions.** The trigger, denominator, horizon and event interpretation are fixed and aligned through propagation.; The joint measure or factorization is explicitly supplied; statistical independence is not inferred solely from graph shape or distinct names.; A represented failure event is equivalent to the modeled violation event, or a residual term/bound records missing coverage. A modeled residual of zero is an assumption requiring justification.; Shared obstacle/domain-hypothesis variables retain identity. Distinct variables may still be statistically correlated.; Point estimates and epistemic distributions retain provenance; numerical error, estimation error and structural omission are kept separate.; The q value comes from an identified requirement/decision source.

**Applicability guard.** A decision genuinely depends on a partial probabilistic satisfaction target, and a meaningful behavior population plus probability model can be specified. If the goal is only qualitative or the model cannot support probabilities, retain P01 and report P02 as inapplicable or unknown.

**Expression or precise operational rule.** **Core.** P02(G,M,q) iff p_M = mu(C intersect H_G)/mu(C) >= q, with mu(C)>0; SV=q-p_M.

**Obstacle reconstruction.** Let V_G be the union of the jointly evaluated modeled obstruction combinations, including needed domain hypotheses. Only if V_G equals the violation event within C may p_M be replaced by 1-mu(V_G|C). Otherwise carry the unmatched failure event/residual bound. Use a joint contingency table, an equivalent probabilistic model, or a correctly weighted Boolean representation; product simplification requires its factorization premises.

**Uncertainty.** For a declared epistemic law Pi over theta, VU(G)=Pi[p_theta(G)<q]. This is uncertainty about meeting the rate threshold, not the operational failure rate. A separate rule such as VU<=alpha is an additional normative decision requiring authorization; it is not silently added to the source's EPS>=RDS rule.

**Bounds.** For a justified model envelope L<=p_M<=U, PASS only if L>=q; FAIL only if U<q; otherwise UNKNOWN. State whether the envelope is deterministic, epistemic or statistical, and do not mislabel one as another.

**Source of the expression.** **Class.** SOURCE_DEFINED_CORE_WITH_RESEARCHER_PROPOSED_OPERATIONAL_GUARDS

**Source ids.** ERE-S-R019; ERE-S-R020

**Source defined.** R019 §3.1 Definitions 1,3–6: nonvacuous finite-count satisfaction, EPS/RDS comparison and signed SV. R020 §III.B: VU as below-RDS probability mass.

**Researcher proposed.** Explicit measure and denominator alignment, joint-dependence guard, residual term, conservative bounds verdicts, evidence partition and examples. These narrow the permissible transfer; they are not attributed as exact historical KAOS rules.

**Observation or measurement map.** Map each recorded episode to C and H_G with a specified observation/censoring rule.; Bind obstacle events to the same eligible population or give an explicit conditional transformation.; Record measurement/elicitation source, counts, selection effects, calibration method if actually performed, and unresolved estimates.; Compare the resulting model calculation with q; report model validity and external predictive support separately.

**Required evidence.** Versioned goal and operationalization of C/H_G.; A03 probability/joint-dependence model and provenance, including unknown/residual cases.; A04 prescribed threshold and its scope/authority.; An explicit calculation or evaluator result with assumptions and numerical precision.; Any empirical calibration or statistical guarantee claimed must have its own data and method; the cited papers alone cannot supply it for a target system.

**Evaluator or reasoning procedure.** **Pass.** The applicable fixed model, or all models in an explicitly justified envelope, yields p>=q. Label PASS_MODEL and preserve assumed/estimated inputs.

**Fail.** The applicable fixed model yields p<q, or a justified envelope lies wholly below q. Label FAIL_MODEL; this is distinct from a directly observed violation.

**Unknown.** Missing/contradictory population, joint law, coverage, threshold, or unresolved uncertainty crosses q; report available conditional computations without claiming empirical assurance.

**Inapplicable.** No quantitative satisfaction threshold is a decision input, or the selected finite probabilistic semantics is inappropriate; name the cheaper path.

**Procedure.** Verify scope and threshold; construct the relevant joint violation event; evaluate p and SV; inspect dependencies/omissions; propagate uncertainty only under an explicit joint uncertainty model; issue a bounded verdict.

**Decidability and approximation.** Finite explicitly enumerated rational models permit exact arithmetic. Finding a faithful goal/domain model is not thereby decidable or guaranteed complete. BDDs may reduce computation but do not create missing probabilities. Monte Carlo gives an approximation whose numerical error and sampling design must be reported independently of elicitation/model error; no numerical error bound was manufactured for this supplement.

**Positive witness.** ERE-CASE-RISK001: a fully specified synthetic 10,000-episode population gives p=0.9702 and q=0.95, so PASS_MODEL with SV=-0.0202.

**Counterexample or failure witness.** ERE-CASE-RISK002: correlated redundant-channel failures produce p=0.92 at q=0.98, while unjustified multiplication reports 0.99. ERE-CASE-RISK003 separately exposes a vacuous denominator.

**Unknown conditions.** Only marginal probabilities supplied where joint probabilities matter; unobserved/censored outcome; nonpositive trigger count; uncertain parameters straddle q; unresolved model coverage or normative threshold.

**Inapplicability conditions.** ERE-CASE-RISK005: low-consequence reversible work with no probabilistic commitment, where a concrete exception/fallback review answers the decision.

**False positive and false negative risks.** Omitted failures, underweighted rare regimes, wrong conditioning, hidden correlation and optimistic expert estimates can produce false passes. Unrepresentative stress data, double-counted shared failures and overly pessimistic unsupported intervals can produce false failures.

**Vacuity or proxy gaming risks.** Counting nontriggering cases as successes; shrinking the admitted population; assigning zero to undiscovered obstacles; assuming independence for convenience; weakening q and calling it performance improvement; using mean EPS to conceal substantial below-threshold epistemic mass.

**Change invalidation rule.** Changes to goal meaning, q, environment, eligibility, horizon, obstacle coverage, shared variables, probability estimates or countermeasures invalidate the affected calculation until rebound to the new version.

**Cost and cheaper alternative.** Use quantitative propagation when decisions depend on threshold or obstacle-priority differences. For a small model, an explicit joint contingency table or sensitivity bounds may suffice. Otherwise a brief feasible-exception review with fallback ownership preserves P01 without spurious numeric assurance.

**Evidence ceiling.** A model-conditional threshold proposition and uncertainty-aware decision aid. It does not establish actual-world probability calibration, completeness of requirements, global safety, regulatory acceptance, or causal field improvement. Source case studies and an author retrospective are not independent replication.

**Formalisation provenance.** **Class.** MIXED_FORMAL_AND_QUALITATIVE

**Source ids.** ERE-S-F011; ERE-S-F010; ERE-S-F023

**Note.** Exact source semantics are named where used; normalized rules, audit tests and counterexamples are researcher constructions, not attributed verbatim.

**Operational evaluation.** **Pass.** Guard true and the stated rule is supported within its explicit scope. For rejected universal candidates, a local positive instance never proves universality.

**Fail.** Guard true and a concrete counterexample or missing mandatory condition defeats the stated claim.

**Unknown.** Guard true but evidence, semantics, authority, model termination or domain correspondence is unresolved.

**Inapplicable.** Guard false with the cheap-path/nontrigger reason documented.

**Procedure.** Seek an independently documented incident or realistic adversarial scenario missing from the model.

**Positive witness or worked example.** A plausible delayed input is linked to a missed deadline and a recovery option with remaining limitations.

**Negative witness or counterexample.** All difficult conditions are declared impossible without environmental evidence.

**Non trigger example.** An irrelevant outage outside the agreed service scope is documented as outside the current analysis.

**Observability and missingness.** Use the two attribute-specific collection methods; distinguish not supplied, examined/unknown and inapplicable.

**Currentness and invalidation.** Change to either attribute, interpretation, source commitment or environment reopens the verdict.

### Evidence limits and open questions

**Evidence ceiling.** Quantitative risk claims require probability/consequence evidence beyond a Boolean obstacle tree. Primary semantics and bounded case evaluations plus a 2025 author retrospective; no independently verified universal calibration or causal field improvement. Mathematical constructions below expose transfer failure modes without alleging real case-data failures.

**Transferability limits.** Obstacles may span traces; a point-state negation must not replace a temporal failure. Coverage is relative to D and search scope. Only the appropriate decision maker may accept a weaker goal or residual exposure

**Unverified or open questions.** Seek an independently documented incident or realistic adversarial scenario missing from the model.

**Next discriminator.** Seek an independently documented incident or realistic adversarial scenario missing from the model.

The packet retains these as related but nonidentical ways to expose a specification that cannot be achieved under the declared interaction model.

**Original terminology.** Vacuity and interesting witnesses occur in the accessible abstract of ERE-S-F018; that abstract-only access supports historical terminology, not an appraisal of its full algorithm. ERE-S-F033 uses vacuity in synthesis, strengthening and witness-based distinctions (introduction and strengthening/witness definitions). 'Discriminating witness checks' also draws on positive and near-miss suites in ERE-S-F037 (§4.1). There is no single source-native term for the packet's combined mechanism.

**Original form.** See exact source/version profiles; the candidate label is a researcher normalization, not an invented historical quotation.

**Original problem.** The motivating failure is a successful formal check or synthesized behavior that does not exercise a meaningful part of the specification. The inspected synthesis treatment examines how witnesses and strengthening distinguish such outcomes (ERE-S-F033, introduction and definitions). Later specification-review suites address intended and near-miss behaviors (ERE-S-F037, §4.1; §6.7 threats). The combined property does not claim that non-vacuity alone recovers stakeholder intent, and it does not infer an unread proof from ERE-S-F018's abstract.

'Control-aware unavoidable conflict classification' is the packet's normalized property name.

**Original form.** See exact source/version profiles; the candidate label is a researcher normalization, not an invented historical quotation.

**Original problem.** ERE-S-F023 challenges boundary-condition generation that produces conditions an appropriately controlled system could avoid, motivating a stronger, decision-relevant classification (introduction; Definition 1; benchmark discussion). The paper's question is whether a conflict condition can be avoided under its interaction model, not whether avoidance is costless, authorized or preferred in an application.

**Branch ids.** ERE-BR-F05; ERE-BR-F04

**Influence or relation class.** Documented source links distinguished from researcher comparisons in genealogy_edges.

**Claim class.** SOURCE_DERIVED

**Bearer or subject.** Domain Dom, goal set and candidate boundary condition φ

**Failure mode or limit addressed.** An available controllable extractor prevents one adverse input under justified domain dynamics, so the same conflict is avoidable.

**Mechanism.** After checking the ordinary boundary-condition properties, test whether avoidance is realizable under the declared control partition.

**Mature or evolved form.** **Predicate ref.** ERE-C0016-P01

**Interpretation.** Control-aware unavoidable conflict classification

**Payoff evidence not just rationale.** Formal definition and benchmark filtering; no measured engineer-time or field-safety effect.

**Alternative mechanisms.** A short explanation, concrete examples, or a targeted review can implement the mechanism without adopting its historical notation.

## ERE-C0017 — Mutual conditional guarantees alone establish progress

### Identity

**Property name.** Mutual conditional guarantees alone establish progress

**Lineage id.** EVOLVED_REQUIREMENTS_ENGINEERING

**Property families.** ERE-FAM10

### Genealogy

**Historical origin.** Criticism-derived composition error; valid circular proof rules have additional hypotheses.

**Original terminology.** There is no single source-native term or documented historical advocate for the claim that mutual conditional guarantees alone establish progress. It is an analyst-created negative sufficiency claim. The native source terms are assume-guarantee contracts (ERE-S-F019, §VII-A), interface compatibility (ERE-S-F020, introduction and definitions), and temporal assumption/guarantee composition (ERE-S-F031, §§5.1–5.2).

### Claim and mechanism

**Engineering claim.** Select information-gathering methods against the unresolved question and source population, preserve the distinction among observation, preference, inference and agreed obligation, and corroborate material discrepancies.

**Claim class.** DEFEASIBLE_METHOD

**Bearer or subject.** An elicitation episode and its resulting candidate claims

**Failure mode or limit addressed.** Accounts of normal work omit tacit practices, exceptions and social constraints.

**Mechanism.** Map questions to accessible sources; use observed activity, dialogue, artifacts or prototypes where each can discriminate a competing interpretation; maintain discrepancies until resolved.

**Mature or evolved form.** Question-driven combination and explicit cheap paths replace method accumulation.

**Expected payoff.** Earlier discovery of material assumptions and exceptions.

**Payoff evidence not just rationale.** Historical methodological rationale and examples; no source here establishes a universally best technique or a necessary number of methods.

**Decision or consumer.** Analyst deciding what can enter a requirements baseline and what inquiry remains.

**Alternative mechanisms.** Existing current document or one direct question to a knowledgeable authorized person; richer contextual study when a concrete blind spot remains.

### Applicability and authority

**Trigger or context.** A material claim depends on tacit practice, disputed vocabulary, exceptions, inaccessible actors or conflicting accounts.

**Non trigger or cheap path.** A reversible wording correction with one known owner and an unambiguous current policy may need only one recorded answer.

**Assumptions and preconditions.** Sources can be accessed lawfully and their statements can be situated; observers recognize that observation can change conduct.

**Environment and boundary.** Declared operation, population, time and decision; observed work is evidence about work, not automatically permission to preserve it.

**Scope and exclusions.** Declared operation, population, time and decision; observed work is evidence about work, not automatically permission to preserve it. Excludes any target repository finding or inter-lineage ownership assignment.

**Authority or normative basis if applicable.** Agreement must be separately evidenced when an observation is promoted into an obligation.

**Input and evidence provenance requirements.** Identify source role, collection method/date, context, direct versus interpreted content and unresolved disagreement.

**Dependencies and conflicts.** **Related property ids.** ERE-C0102; ERE-C0111

**Tension ids.** ERE-T-S01; ERE-T-S02

**Limit.** Relations are conditional; see internal_relations, not all listed items are mandatory prerequisites

**Failure of assumptions.** A workshop statement becomes a mandatory requirement although field observations contradict it and neither source nor interpretation is retained.

**Cost and maintenance burden.** Field access, transcription, interpretation and participant effort; richer observation justified by a decision it may change.

**Retirement or reentry condition.** Stop when material rival interpretations are resolved or explicitly bounded for the decision; reopen on a new role, exception or conflicting observation.

### Criticism and evolution

**Criticism ids.** ERE-CR-S01

**Strongest objection.** Triangulation can multiply correlated opinions; an intrusive field study can cost more than it reveals.

**Known failures and misuses.** A workshop statement becomes a mandatory requirement although field observations contradict it and neither source nor interpretation is retained.

**Response or descendant form.** Question-driven combination and explicit cheap paths replace method accumulation.

**What changed and what did not.** Preserves situated discovery; narrows corroboration to material uncertainty and declared populations.

**Residual limits.** Unseen practices, inaccessible people and researcher interpretation remain; no numerical saturation guarantee.

**Ceremony versus mechanism.** Number of interviews or workshops is not the mechanism; a discriminating observation or short answer may be enough.

**Internal tension ids.** ERE-T-S01; ERE-T-S02

**Retention status.** RETAINED_IN_EVOLVED_FORM

**Retention rationale.** Retain the bounded mechanism with explicit guard, evidence and cheap path. Question-driven combination and explicit cheap paths replace method accumulation.

### Predicates, witnesses and evaluation

**Predicate specifications.** **Predicate id.** ERE-C0101-P01

**Property id.** ERE-C0101

**Name and plain language claim.** Select information-gathering methods against the unresolved question and source population, preserve the distinction among observation, preference, inference and agreed obligation, and corroborate material discrepancies.

**Predicate kind.** QUALITATIVE_ASSESSMENT

**Evaluation mode.** **Mode.** HUMAN_IN_THE_LOOP_OPERATIONAL_RULE

**Definition.** Mode describes how evidence is assessed, separate from the commissioned predicate-role enum. A sufficiency challenge tests an asserted implication or universal process benefit; ordinary operational assessment evaluates the bounded source-informed rule. Mechanical record checks do not settle semantic, empirical or authority judgments.

**Subject and argument signature.** Assess(subject: An elicitation episode and its resulting candidate claims, context, consumerDecision, evidenceSnapshot, validTime) -> PASS|FAIL|UNKNOWN|INAPPLICABLE

**Variable domains and units.** **Attribute id.** ERE-C0101-A01

**Domain.** enum

**Constraint.** OBSERVED_WORKAROUND|STATED_PREFERENCE|ANALYST_INFERENCE|AGREED_OBLIGATION

**Attribute id.** ERE-C0101-A02

**Domain.** set of named gaps

**Constraint.** Each gap names consequence and next discriminator

**Quantifiers and scope.** Universal only over explicitly enumerated material items needed for the declared decision and search scope. No quantification over all possible stakeholders, worlds or future changes. A universal sufficiency claim is refuted by a valid applicable counterexample; case PASS is not universal proof.

PASS denotes this bounded inquiry discipline, not discovery of every possible need.

**False positive and false negative risks.** **False positive.** Number of interviews or workshops is not the mechanism; a discriminating observation or short answer may be enough.

**False negative.** Rejecting a legitimate cheap path, demanding irrelevant evidence, or treating an unrecorded but unresolved dimension as known false.

**Change invalidation rule.** New operating shift, affected population or changed practice invalidates the relevant coverage claim even when requirement wording is unchanged.

### Evidence limits and open questions

**Transferability limits.** Declared operation, population, time and decision; observed work is evidence about work, not automatically permission to preserve it. Unseen practices, inaccessible people and researcher interpretation remain; no numerical saturation guarantee.

### Claim and mechanism

**Engineering claim.** For a consequential requirement decision, distinguish who is affected, who supplied evidence, who represents whom, and who can bind which organization; preserve dissent and reopening conditions.

**Claim class.** EVIDENCE_AND_AUTHORITY_DISCIPLINE

**Bearer or subject.** A requirements decision with a declared affected population

**Failure mode or limit addressed.** Present or powerful participants are mistaken for all affected people; technical knowledge is mistaken for decision rights.

**Mechanism.** Use role/lifecycle and interaction searches to challenge coverage; record proxy limits, decision remit, competing interests and the disposition that authorized the chosen obligation.

**Mature or evolved form.** Treat taxonomy as discovery heuristic and record uncertainty/challenge rights; do not turn the resulting network into a legitimacy score. WinWin-descended preference analysis can structure options and sensitivity, but it does not guarantee agreement or settle rightful representation.

**Expected payoff.** Decisions can be challenged on representation and authority rather than hidden in a priority weight.

**Payoff evidence not just rationale.** Conceptual methods and current political-model proposals support the problem framing; Sharp explicitly reports no validation, and PEN only retrospective reinterpretations.

**Decision or consumer.** Decision-maker, affected-party representative and downstream implementer.

**Alternative mechanisms.** For a single-owner private task, record that owner’s request and scope; use facilitated negotiation for unresolved cross-party conflicts.

### Applicability and authority

**Trigger or context.** More than one affected role, absent constituency, surrogate, conflict, delegated decision or binding external commitment.

**Non trigger or cheap path.** A sole owner requests a reversible local change and no material external effect is identified after a scoped check.

**Assumptions and preconditions.** Affect and decision remit can be examined; any legitimate authority source is available and current.

**Environment and boundary.** Coverage is relative to explicit system/lifecycle/context boundaries; power and graph centrality are descriptive, not automatic normative weights.

**Scope and exclusions.** Coverage is relative to explicit system/lifecycle/context boundaries; power and graph centrality are descriptive, not automatic normative weights. Excludes any target repository finding or inter-lineage ownership assignment.

**Authority or normative basis if applicable.** Authority is a witnessed remit (role, delegation, policy, contract or applicable norm), separate from expertise, interest, consent and empirical truth.

**Input and evidence provenance requirements.** Source of role and remit; represented population; proxy selection; exclusions; dissent; actual decision record.

**Dependencies and conflicts.** **Related property ids.** ERE-C0101; ERE-C0103; ERE-C0113

**Tension ids.** ERE-T-S01; ERE-T-S03

**Limit.** Relations are conditional; see internal_relations, not all listed items are mandatory prerequisites

**Failure of assumptions.** The sponsor and vendor agree unanimously while excluded night staff and patients bear consequences; the record labels consensus complete and binding on them.

**Cost and maintenance burden.** Recruitment, access, negotiation and continuing role-currentness; exhaustive social graphs can swamp the team.

**Retirement or reentry condition.** Bound the search when open exclusions cannot change the current decision under stated assumptions; reopen on new affected groups, mandate change or disputed representation.

### Criticism and evolution

**Criticism ids.** ERE-CR-S02

**Strongest objection.** No taxonomy can guarantee inclusion; power can distort consent; documenting a proxy does not make representation legitimate.

**Known failures and misuses.** The sponsor and vendor agree unanimously while excluded night staff and patients bear consequences; the record labels consensus complete and binding on them.

**Response or descendant form.** Treat taxonomy as discovery heuristic and record uncertainty/challenge rights; do not turn the resulting network into a legitimacy score. WinWin-descended preference analysis can structure options and sensitivity, but it does not guarantee agreement or settle rightful representation.

**What changed and what did not.** Makes completeness and authority explicit claims with witnesses; retains irreducible political disagreement.

**Residual limits.** Legitimate competing interests may have no technical resolution; supplied mandate can itself be disputed.

**Ceremony versus mechanism.** Signatures, full meeting attendance or high stakeholder weights cannot substitute for representation and scope.

**Internal tension ids.** ERE-T-S01; ERE-T-S03

**Retention status.** STRONGLY_RETAINED

**Retention rationale.** Retain the bounded mechanism with explicit guard, evidence and cheap path. Treat taxonomy as discovery heuristic and record uncertainty/challenge rights; do not turn the resulting network into a legitimacy score. WinWin-descended preference analysis can structure options and sensitivity, but it does not guarantee agreement or settle rightful representation.

### Claim and mechanism

**Engineering claim.** Preserve locally owned partial specifications and their history; make cross-viewpoint relations and inconsistency disposition explicit at the decision where consistency matters.

**Failure mode or limit addressed.** A single prematurely uniform specification hides partial knowledge, incompatible vocabularies and unresolved conflicts.

**Mechanism.** Separate owner and representation from content; define inter-viewpoint consistency conditions; tolerate labeled provisional inconsistency during exploration but require resolution or bounded exception at the consuming decision.

**Mature or evolved form.** Use only decision-relevant views and explicit cross-view contracts; do not require perpetual global consistency.

### Applicability and authority

**Trigger or context.** Heterogeneous representations, multiple owners, changing or inconsistent partial knowledge.

**Environment and boundary.** Consistency applies to named relations, versions and stage; legitimate difference in preference is not automatically a logical contradiction.

**Scope and exclusions.** Consistency applies to named relations, versions and stage; legitimate difference in preference is not automatically a logical contradiction. Excludes any target repository finding or inter-lineage ownership assignment.

**Authority or normative basis if applicable.** Viewpoint ownership confers maintenance responsibility, not automatic power to decide another actor’s interests.

**Retirement or reentry condition.** Retire a view only when its concerns have a current consumer/owner elsewhere; reopen affected consistency checks after change.

### Criticism and evolution

**Criticism ids.** ERE-CR-S03

**Strongest objection.** Maintaining many views can multiply drift, cost and inscrutable integration rules.

**Known failures and misuses.** A merge deletes operations’ disconnected-work assumption to make two documents superficially consistent.

**Response or descendant form.** Use only decision-relevant views and explicit cross-view contracts; do not require perpetual global consistency.

**What changed and what did not.** Preserves local partiality; distinguishes transient contradiction from release-critical incompatibility.

**Residual limits.** Syntactic or logical consistency still cannot establish correct domain facts or rightful authority.

**Ceremony versus mechanism.** View count and a clean merged diagram are weak proxies for shared understanding.

**Internal tension ids.** ERE-T-S03

**Retention status.** CONTEXT_DEPENDENT

**Engineering claim.** Use declared notation/version and relation semantics, distinguish attributed intention from evidence, and validate every downstream translation separately from source-model well-formedness.

**Expected payoff.** Auditable analysis of dependence, vulnerability and alternatives without semantic mixing.

**Payoff evidence not just rationale.** Detailed primary definitions and illustrative applications; current generation experiments support bounded automation only, not organizational truth or refinement correctness.

**Trigger or context.** Multiple actor dependencies, conflicting goals, alternative means or intentional-model automation/translation.

### Criticism and evolution

**Criticism ids.** ERE-CR-S04

**Strongest objection.** Actor intentions are partial interpretations and models can be expensive; syntax checks and smell correction reward the chosen notation more than faithful social explanation.

**Known failures and misuses.** A tool interprets Help as a fixed additive probability and declares an organization committed because an analyst drew a dependency.

**Response or descendant form.** Limit model scope to an explicit question; distinguish integrity, attribution, reasoning and real-world satisfaction; preserve competing interpretations.

**What changed and what did not.** iStar 2.0 restricts a common core and replaces hard/soft distinction with goal/quality categories; Tropos extends into lifecycle activities but neither change proves correctness of social assumptions.

**Residual limits.** Scale, content validation, precise effect of weak contributions and real-world power/trust remain context-dependent.

**Ceremony versus mechanism.** A large diagram, correct JSON or absence of smells is not evidence that the modeled parties intended or authorized the relation.

**Retention status.** RETAINED_IN_EVOLVED_FORM

**Inapplicability conditions.** An analyst sketches a possible supplier relation explicitly labeled hypothetical.

**False positive and false negative risks.** **False positive.** Graph completeness is incapable of substituting for the missing external evidence.

**False negative.** Rejecting a legitimate cheap path, demanding irrelevant evidence, or treating an unrecorded but unresolved dimension as known false.

**Vacuity or proxy gaming risks.** An empty declared scope cannot pass merely because no obligations were listed: explain why the guard is inapplicable or why the scope is adequate. Graph completeness is incapable of substituting for the missing external evidence.

**Change invalidation rule.** Revoked agreement, lost capacity or changed scope invalidates external facts independently of unchanged graph syntax.

**Cost and cheaper alternative.** Separate witness collection can be minimal; omitting it falsely saves work by changing the claim. Alternative: A graph used only to explore a hypothetical relation needs no actual-delivery evidence, but must retain hypothetical status.

**Evidence ceiling.** The supplied semantics do not entail those external assertions; a concrete same-graph/different-world counterexample defeats universal sufficiency. The operational rule is a proposed audit discriminator, not a measured process-effect claim.

**Formalisation provenance.** Analytical operational reconstruction from inspected primary sources; no claim of a source-native theorem or universal algorithm.

**Operational evaluation.** **Rule.** For the proposed implication EdgeWellFormed ⇒ Consent∧Authority∧Capability∧Delivered, a case with EdgeWellFormed and a false consequent is FAIL. Confirming all consequent facts gives only bounded case PASS, never universal sufficiency. Missing external witnesses yields UNKNOWN; an edge used solely as hypothetical analysis is INAPPLICABLE.

**Outcomes.** **Pass.** Required evidence supports the bounded claim within scope; no universal extrapolation

**Fail.** An applicable observed contradiction, failed criterion or valid counterexample defeats the specified claim

**Unknown.** Relevant evidence/meaning/authority is missing, disputed or not discriminating

**Inapplicable.** An explicit guard excludes the claim; cheap path must be justified

**Empty scope rule.** Empty obligation/source sets never establish completeness by vacuity; show scope adequacy or label inapplicable/unknown.

**Positive witness or worked example.** A separately signed and scoped agreement plus capability assessment and delivery observation supports the four external facts for one case; the graph is an index to that evidence.

**Negative witness or counterexample.** The same well-formed pharmacy-delivery dependency is drawn in two worlds; in one the supplier has declined and has no available stock. Graph identity does not entail agreement or ability.

**Non trigger example.** An analyst sketches a possible supplier relation explicitly labeled hypothetical.

**Observability and missingness.** External confirmation, remit, capacity evidence and actual outcome record, each with date/configuration. Missing evidence remains UNKNOWN unless an explicit contradicted claim is being tested.

**Currentness and invalidation.** Revoked agreement, lost capacity or changed scope invalidates external facts independently of unchanged graph syntax.

### Evidence limits and open questions

**Evidence ceiling.** The supplied semantics do not entail those external assertions; a concrete same-graph/different-world counterexample defeats universal sufficiency. Source access levels bind every claim; schema completeness is not domain validation.

**Transferability limits.** Counterexample is analytical, not an empirical incident; a contractual rule could add authority, but that is extra evidence. Even a current agreement may be breached; capability is conditional and delivery requires observation.

**Unverified or open questions.** Only an explicit additional semantics/witness linking an edge to a binding and observed world state could narrow this rejection.

**Next discriminator.** Only an explicit additional semantics/witness linking an edge to a binding and observed world state could narrow this rejection.

### Claim and mechanism

**Engineering claim.** Operationalize a quality with its affected population, stimulus/environment, response, observation and criterion authority; retain uncertainty, excluded dimensions and anti-gaming conditions.

**Claim class.** CONTEXTUAL_MEASUREMENT_AND_AUTHORITY

**Bearer or subject.** A quality criterion and the phenomenon it is intended to represent

**Failure mode or limit addressed.** Words such as fast or usable are unverifiable; precise proxies can omit the users or failures that gave the concern meaning.

**Mechanism.** Define the scenario, denominator/population, units, time window and response measure; justify proxy-to-concern correspondence; record who set the target and review trade-offs.

**Mature or evolved form.** Use a scenario-bound measure and keep qualitative concerns and adverse effects explicit; avoid forced weighted sums.

**Expected payoff.** Comparable engineering decisions and observable criteria without silently replacing the intended quality.

**Payoff evidence not just rationale.** Primary scenario method and taxonomy plus bounded BDD performance case; no general empirical threshold or universal proxy validity demonstrated.

**Decision or consumer.** Architect, tester, operator and receiving stakeholder deciding acceptable quality.

**Alternative mechanisms.** Structured expert judgment with declared uncertainty when valid numeric measurement is unavailable; prototype/task observation for usability.

### Applicability and authority

**Trigger or context.** A vague or conflicting quality concern influences design or acceptance.

**Non trigger or cheap path.** A directly observable binary event with agreed scope may require a simple criterion, not a multi-attribute scorecard.

**Assumptions and preconditions.** The measurement population and environment are observable; proxy validity and target choice are treated as separate claims.

**Environment and boundary.** Measured response in a selected scenario; external validity does not extend automatically to other users, load or failures.

**Scope and exclusions.** Measured response in a selected scenario; external validity does not extend automatically to other users, load or failures. Excludes any target repository finding or inter-lineage ownership assignment.

**Authority or normative basis if applicable.** A chosen SLA/acceptance target is a governance decision; it is not a scientifically established universal boundary.

**Input and evidence provenance requirements.** Concern owner, source of threshold, measurement method, excluded cases, units, instrument and calibration/uncertainty.

**Dependencies and conflicts.** **Related property ids.** ERE-C0102; ERE-C0107; ERE-C0113

**Tension ids.** ERE-T-S05; ERE-T-S06

**Limit.** Relations are conditional; see internal_relations, not all listed items are mandatory prerequisites

**Failure of assumptions.** The system drops slow requests; latency of completed requests improves while users receive fewer successful results. The old metric alone wrongly certifies quality.

**Cost and maintenance burden.** Instrumentation, representative sampling and checking distribution/denominator changes; precision can cost more than the decision warrants.

**Retirement or reentry condition.** Revisit the criterion on new population/load, proxy behavior, adverse trade-off or changed threshold authority.

### Criticism and evolution

**Criticism ids.** ERE-CR-S06

**Strongest objection.** Quantification can erase material qualitative aspects and introduce incentives to optimize the proxy.

**Known failures and misuses.** The system drops slow requests; latency of completed requests improves while users receive fewer successful results. The old metric alone wrongly certifies quality.

**Response or descendant form.** Use a scenario-bound measure and keep qualitative concerns and adverse effects explicit; avoid forced weighted sums.

**What changed and what did not.** Refines vague concerns into bounded criteria while rejecting precision as a substitute for meaning.

**Residual limits.** Some qualities remain disputed and indirectly observable; operational precision does not eliminate value judgments.

**Ceremony versus mechanism.** A dashboard with precise units and green thresholds can still measure the wrong population.

**Internal tension ids.** ERE-T-S05; ERE-T-S06

**Retention status.** USEFUL_BUT_EASILY_GAMED

**Retention rationale.** Retain the bounded mechanism with explicit guard, evidence and cheap path. Use a scenario-bound measure and keep qualitative concerns and adverse effects explicit; avoid forced weighted sums.

Numeric aggregation without a justified mapping FAILS. Human assessment may yield UNKNOWN for a contested effect rather than forcing a score.

**Outcomes.** **Pass.** Required evidence supports the bounded claim within scope; no universal extrapolation

**Fail.** An applicable observed contradiction, failed criterion or valid counterexample defeats the specified claim

**Unknown.** Relevant evidence/meaning/authority is missing, disputed or not discriminating

**Inapplicable.** An explicit guard excludes the claim; cheap path must be justified

**Empty scope rule.** Empty obligation/source sets never establish completeness by vacuity; show scope adequacy or label inapplicable/unknown.

**Positive witness or worked example.** Caching helps response time but may hurt freshness; measured workload and stale-data risks are recorded and a scoped choice is authorized.

**Negative witness or counterexample.** Help is assigned +1 and Hurt −1 without evidence; the highest total is declared objectively best and acceptable to every stakeholder.

**Non trigger example.** An agreed checksum-format constraint is directly checkable and has no relevant qualitative trade-off.

**Observability and missingness.** Argument graph/table, measured supporting observations, dissent and defeated assumptions. Missing evidence remains UNKNOWN unless an explicit contradicted claim is being tested.

**Currentness and invalidation.** Change to contribution evidence or interaction context invalidates propagated conclusions and selected trade-off.

### Evidence limits and open questions

**Evidence ceiling.** Foundational framework and worked examples provide reasoning rationale; formal-semantic and real-size validation limits explicitly admitted in 1992. Source access levels bind every claim; schema completeness is not domain validation.

**Transferability limits.** Weak contribution is not a probability, magnitude or universal effect; Make/Break semantics belong to a named model and premises. Judgment disagreement and interaction effects may remain irreducible; evidence may support only direction.

**Unverified or open questions.** Independently test the pivotal contribution under the chosen scenario, or expose how reversing it changes the decision.

**Next discriminator.** Independently test the pivotal contribution under the chosen scenario, or expose how reversing it changes the decision.

**Required evidence.** Original statement, selected template/version, semantic interpretation and reviewer/source for changed meaning.

**Evaluator or reasoning procedure.** An informed evaluator checks applicability, identifies the exact claim and scope, reviews the named witnesses, tests the supplied counterexample class and records a reasoned four-valued outcome. Mechanical schema checks can establish presence/identity, not domain truth or authority.

**Decidability and approximation.** Finite record checks are mechanically decidable. Semantic correspondence, legitimate representation, proxy validity and causal transfer generally require contextual judgment and may remain UNKNOWN. No claim of general decidability.

**Positive witness.** **Class.** ANALYTICAL_CONSTRUCTION_UNLESS_SOURCE_EXPLICITLY_IDENTIFIED

**Text.** A command-triggered response explicitly names the trigger, relevant state, system and response, with a domain expert confirming the interpretation.

**Case ids.** ERE-CASE-S11

**Counterexample or failure witness.** **Class.** ANALYTICAL_CONSTRUCTION

**Text.** An author removes an exception to fit a simpler template; the sentence is grammatical but changes the required behavior.

**Unknown conditions.** The guard plausibly applies but required source, semantic interpretation, authority, context or observation is missing/disputed; insufficient evidence is not silently coded FAIL or PASS.

**Inapplicability conditions.** A fixed export-format constraint is already precise and a template adds no useful information.

**False positive and false negative risks.** **False positive.** The modal verb and occupied slots are not a full requirement-quality test.

**False negative.** Rejecting a legitimate cheap path, demanding irrelevant evidence, or treating an unrecorded but unresolved dimension as known false.

**Vacuity or proxy gaming risks.** An empty declared scope cannot pass merely because no obligations were listed: explain why the guard is inapplicable or why the scope is adequate. The modal verb and occupied slots are not a full requirement-quality test.

**Change invalidation rule.** Changed pattern version or trigger/exception/domain definition requires renewed meaning-preservation assessment.

**Cost and cheaper alternative.** Training, semantic preservation review and template edge cases; novice rewriting can damage meaning. Alternative: A short unambiguous static constraint can stay a direct sentence if all consumers understand it.

**Evidence ceiling.** Human/domain correspondence judgment tied to the original statement and current sources; no claim of general semantic-equivalence decidability or universal template benefit.

**Formalisation provenance.** Analytical operational reconstruction from inspected primary sources; no claim of a source-native theorem or universal algorithm.

**Operational evaluation.** **Rule.** Given a fitting requirement type, check explicit slots and pattern use, then separately assess meaning preservation. Syntax PASS alone does not pass the semantic review; unknown domain terms or an unreviewed substantive rewrite yield UNKNOWN for meaning.

**Outcomes.** **Pass.** Required evidence supports the bounded claim within scope; no universal extrapolation

**Fail.** An applicable observed contradiction, failed criterion or valid counterexample defeats the specified claim

**Unknown.** Relevant evidence/meaning/authority is missing, disputed or not discriminating

**Inapplicable.** An explicit guard excludes the claim; cheap path must be justified

**Empty scope rule.** Empty obligation/source sets never establish completeness by vacuity; show scope adequacy or label inapplicable/unknown.

**Positive witness or worked example.** A command-triggered response explicitly names the trigger, relevant state, system and response, with a domain expert confirming the interpretation.

**Negative witness or counterexample.** An author removes an exception to fit a simpler template; the sentence is grammatical but changes the required behavior.

**Non trigger example.** A fixed export-format constraint is already precise and a template adds no useful information.

**Observability and missingness.** Statement pair, pattern grammar and semantic review with source terminology. Missing evidence remains UNKNOWN unless an explicit contradicted claim is being tested.

**Currentness and invalidation.** Changed pattern version or trigger/exception/domain definition requires renewed meaning-preservation assessment.

### Evidence limits and open questions

**Evidence ceiling.** Original small author case and2024 comparisons support selected linguistic effects; neither establishes necessity, feasibility or global completeness. Source access levels bind every claim; schema completeness is not domain validation.

**Transferability limits.** Original2009 high-level stakeholder focus; Adv-EARS and other templates are separate systems. Lexical ambiguity, unknown requirements, feasibility and authority remain outside the template.

**Unverified or open questions.** Ask actual readers to use the original/rewrite for the intended downstream task and check meaning errors, not merely lint scores.

**Next discriminator.** Ask actual readers to use the original/rewrite for the intended downstream task and check meaning errors, not merely lint scores.

**Decidability and approximation.** Finite record checks are mechanically decidable. Semantic correspondence, legitimate representation, proxy validity and causal transfer generally require contextual judgment and may remain UNKNOWN. No claim of general decidability.

**Positive witness.** **Class.** ANALYTICAL_CONSTRUCTION_UNLESS_SOURCE_EXPLICITLY_IDENTIFIED

**Text.** A changed notification timing assumption marks linked requirement, test oracle and acceptance decision for review even though their IDs remain unchanged.

**Counterexample or failure witness.** **Class.** ANALYTICAL_CONSTRUCTION

**Text.** The requirement now covers all customers but the linked test still samples only active accounts; a complete matrix falsely reports coverage.

**Unknown conditions.** The guard plausibly applies but required source, semantic interpretation, authority, context or observation is missing/disputed; insufficient evidence is not silently coded FAIL or PASS.

**Inapplicability conditions.** A one-off personal text correction is fully evidenced by the request and direct resulting diff.

**False positive and false negative risks.** **False positive.** A filled matrix, stable identifier or large number of edges is not the mechanism.

**False negative.** Rejecting a legitimate cheap path, demanding irrelevant evidence, or treating an unrecorded but unresolved dimension as known false.

**Vacuity or proxy gaming risks.** An empty declared scope cannot pass merely because no obligations were listed: explain why the guard is inapplicable or why the scope is adequate. A filled matrix, stable identifier or large number of edges is not the mechanism.

**Change invalidation rule.** Changed source meaning, actor authority, environment, target behavior or consumer query invalidates relevant relation assurance.

**Cost and cheaper alternative.** Link creation and ongoing review; benefits and costs often fall on different people. Alternative: Short-lived single-person reversible work with one obvious source and no foreseeable downstream impact may need one note/link.

**Evidence ceiling.** Historical practitioner investigation and2023/2016 field reports identify practical needs and burdens; controlled maintenance benefits are abstract-only here, not promoted. The operational rule is a proposed audit discriminator, not a measured process-effect claim.

**Formalisation provenance.** Analytical operational reconstruction from inspected primary sources; no claim of a source-native theorem or universal algorithm.

**Operational evaluation.** **Rule.** A relied-on trace passes only if its typed relation has a semantic witness at the specified versions/context and can answer its declared consumer query. Known stale/spurious relation FAILS; missing review after material change is UNKNOWN. Connectivity or matching IDs is never the witness.

**Outcomes.** **Pass.** Required evidence supports the bounded claim within scope; no universal extrapolation

**Fail.** An applicable observed contradiction, failed criterion or valid counterexample defeats the specified claim

**Unknown.** Relevant evidence/meaning/authority is missing, disputed or not discriminating

**Inapplicable.** An explicit guard excludes the claim; cheap path must be justified

**Empty scope rule.** Empty obligation/source sets never establish completeness by vacuity; show scope adequacy or label inapplicable/unknown.

**Negative witness or counterexample.** The requirement now covers all customers but the linked test still samples only active accounts; a complete matrix falsely reports coverage.

**Non trigger example.** A one-off personal text correction is fully evidenced by the request and direct resulting diff.

**Observability and missingness.** Link record, query result, version/context differences, rationale and reviewer/source confirmation. Missing evidence remains UNKNOWN unless an explicit contradicted claim is being tested.

**Currentness and invalidation.** Changed source meaning, actor authority, environment, target behavior or consumer query invalidates relevant relation assurance.

### Evidence limits and open questions

**Evidence ceiling.** Historical practitioner investigation and2023/2016 field reports identify practical needs and burdens; controlled maintenance benefits are abstract-only here, not promoted. Source access levels bind every claim; schema completeness is not domain validation.

**Transferability limits.** A link is relative to its semantic type, granularity and current context; unchanged source text may support a changed meaning poorly. Unrecorded tacit knowledge and inaccessible people can still defeat retrieval; unknown future queries cannot all be anticipated.

**Unverified or open questions.** Test representative change questions against the maintained links and compare result quality plus maintenance effort with a cheaper method.

**Next discriminator.** Test representative change questions against the maintained links and compare result quality plus maintenance effort with a cheaper method.

**Text.** The application reports email queued and all unit tests pass, but the downstream provider rejects the address and no user is notified; external notification remains failed.

**Unknown conditions.** The guard plausibly applies but required source, semantic interpretation, authority, context or observation is missing/disputed; insufficient evidence is not silently coded FAIL or PASS.

**Inapplicability conditions.** A private static-format output with one receiving user and no external dependency is settled by direct content inspection.

**False positive and false negative risks.** **False positive.** A green test suite and signed checklist are indexes to evidence, not substitutes for it.

**False negative.** Rejecting a legitimate cheap path, demanding irrelevant evidence, or treating an unrecorded but unresolved dimension as known false.

**Vacuity or proxy gaming risks.** An empty declared scope cannot pass merely because no obligations were listed: explain why the guard is inapplicable or why the scope is adequate. A green test suite and signed checklist are indexes to evidence, not substitutes for it.

**Change invalidation rule.** Changed build, data population, external service, criterion or receiving remit reopens the corresponding evidence dimension.

**Cost and cheaper alternative.** Independent observations only when they resolve a material remaining claim; redundant reviews can add burden without changing evidence. Alternative: A user requests a private file with specified content; inspection of that exact file under the agreed criterion may settle the decision.

**Evidence ceiling.** Field requirement/test-documentation problems and bounded operational cases support the need for distinct links; no claim this combined schema itself has trial-proven effectiveness. The operational rule is a proposed audit discriminator, not a measured process-effect claim.

**Formalisation provenance.** Analytical operational reconstruction from inspected primary sources; no claim of a source-native theorem or universal algorithm.

**Operational evaluation.** **Rule.** Evaluate each required dimension separately as PASS/FAIL/UNKNOWN/INAPPLICABLE. The consuming decision may PASS only under its declared rule over those statuses and current authority; an observed contradiction FAILS the affected dimension. A passed local test cannot fill UNKNOWN external-outcome or representation cells.

**Outcomes.** **Pass.** Required evidence supports the bounded claim within scope; no universal extrapolation

**Fail.** An applicable observed contradiction, failed criterion or valid counterexample defeats the specified claim

**Unknown.** Relevant evidence/meaning/authority is missing, disputed or not discriminating

**Inapplicable.** An explicit guard excludes the claim; cheap path must be justified

**Empty scope rule.** Empty obligation/source sets never establish completeness by vacuity; show scope adequacy or label inapplicable/unknown.

**Positive witness or worked example.** A delivery service verifies message enqueueing, then separately observes recipient receipt in the relevant channel; the receiving owner accepts only the supported service scope.

**Negative witness or counterexample.** The application reports email queued and all unit tests pass, but the downstream provider rejects the address and no user is notified; external notification remains failed.

**Non trigger example.** A private static-format output with one receiving user and no external dependency is settled by direct content inspection.

**Observability and missingness.** Test traces, observed outcomes, criterion mapping, negative-case checks and scoped acceptance decision. Missing evidence remains UNKNOWN unless an explicit contradicted claim is being tested.

**Currentness and invalidation.** Changed build, data population, external service, criterion or receiving remit reopens the corresponding evidence dimension.

### Evidence limits and open questions

**Evidence ceiling.** Field requirement/test-documentation problems and bounded operational cases support the need for distinct links; no claim this combined schema itself has trial-proven effectiveness. Source access levels bind every claim; schema completeness is not domain validation.

**Transferability limits.** Conformance, validity, outcome and acceptance are distinct even when one observation informs several; none automatically entails all others. An authorized party can accept residual risk without making an unsupported proposition true; latent outcomes may remain unobserved.

**Unverified or open questions.** Use a negative control or changed external assumption that preserves local tests and see whether the acceptance conclusion is properly revised.

**Next discriminator.** Use a negative control or changed external assumption that preserves local tests and see whether the acceptance conclusion is properly revised.
